등교 시 진행되는 캠페인 참여를 독려하려고
학교 시설 개방 시간의 변경을 공지하려고

questions.script:
W: Good afternoon, students. This is your vice principal, Ms. Emily
Johnson. I’d like to let you know about an important update to our
school entrances. Starting next Monday, the current main entrance
will be permanently closed as part of a safety improvement project.
Instead, a new entrance on the south side of the school will be
opened as the main entrance. All students should enter and exit the
school through this new entrance. Signs will be posted to guide you,
and staff members will be there to assist during busy times. Please
remember to use the new entrance for your safety and convenience.
Thank you for your cooperation.

인공 지능이 자신만의 음악을 만드는 데 도움이 된다.
인공 지능을 활용한 창작 시 저작권법 준수가 필수적이다.
questions.script:

W: Yeah, I did. I was surprised to learn that you made the song
yourself.
M: Actually, AI helped me make it.
W: I thought songs made by AI sound the same. Doesn’t it just copy
other original songs?
M: No. AI can actually help you create personalized music.
W: You mean you can create your own songs with AI?
M: Exactly. All you have to do is put in the styles of melodies or
moods you want.
W: Oh, then AI would make me a song that reflects my preferences. So
it’s a kind of assistant.
M: Yes. Using AI helps you make your own music.
W: Sounds great. I’ll try it later.

questions.script:
W: Hello, everyone! It’s Amy from Bright Morning Radio. While on the
bus or subway, what do you do? Most of you check emails, read
books, or listen to language lessons. However, do you think it’s
really good for you? Simply doing nothing while on public
transportation can be very helpful for your brain. According to some
research, it allows your brain a rare chance to rest and truly
recharge. In our busy lives, that might be the only time during the
day when we can pause and clear our mind. So, next time you’re on
public transportation, give your brain a break. Try doing nothing, so
you can refresh your mind and save your energy.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 그림에서 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
questions.script:
W: Hi, Richard. I heard your dad retired last week. Did you do
something special for him?
M: I did. We recently had a family gathering at a small hall we rented.
I took a picture of the place.
W: Let me see. Oh, you put a “Congratulations!” banner on the wall.
M: Yeah, we hung it high so everyone could see it.
W: There is a screen in the corner. What was it for?
M: We played a video of his memories on it. Dad loved it.
W: That sounds really nice. And I see two flower pots near the screen.
M: Right. That type of flower is my dad’s favorite.
W: And what’s that stripe­patterned box on the table?
M: It was a gift for Dad. We all prepared it together.
W: Cool. And there’s a microphone stand next to the table.
M: Yeah, we used it when we shared a few words about him.
W: Everything looks so warm and meaningful. I’m sure your dad was
truly touched.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

questions.script:
M: Abbey, our mini orchestra concert is next week. I’m so excited!
W: So am I! But I’m worried we might have missed something
important.
M: Don’t worry. Let’s go through the checklist together. First of all,
you got permission to use the school assembly hall, right?
W: Yes, I did. And did you send the invitations out to parents?
M: I sent them all last week. What about the posters?
W: The first graders put them on the bulletin board this morning.
M: Great! Oh, I think I forgot to check the sound system.
W: No worries. Our teacher and I already checked it. It’s working
perfectly.
M: Looks like we’re almost ready then.
W: Oh, one more thing! We need to check if the chairs for the
audience are set up properly.
M: Sure, I’ll check and let you know.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
questions.script:
M: Welcome to Forest Botanical Garden.
W: Hello, I’d like to purchase admission tickets for my family.
M: Sure. Tickets are $20 for adults and $15 for children. How many
tickets would you like?
W: I’ll take two adults and two children tickets.
M: Great. There’s also a guided tour available for an extra $5 per
person. You can learn about the various plants in our garden.
W: No, thanks. We don’t need it. Do you have a local residents
discount? I think I saw it on your website.
M: Of course, 10% is discounted from the total for locals. Do you live
in the area?
W: Yes, we do. I brought our identification cards. Here they are.
M: Okay, thank you. So, that’s two adults and two children tickets, plus
a 10% discount.
W: Yes, that’s right. Here’s my credit card.

W: That sounds cool. Where does it take place?
M: It’s going to be held at the Astro Science Center.
W: Oh, that’s not far from school. When is the camp?

questions.prompt: 2026 Beeswax Lip Balm Event에 관한 다음 내용을 듣고, 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 2일 동안 진행된다.
다큐멘터리가 상영된다.
꿀로 만든 간식이 제공된다.
참가비는 무료이다.
참가 인원은 100명으로 제한된다.
questions.script:
M: Hello, listeners! Are you looking for a meaningful way to learn
about the environment and create something useful? I’m excited to
invite you to the 2026 Beeswax Lip Balm Event! It’ll last two days,
from September 2nd to the 3rd at 10 a.m. at City Plaza. During the
event, we’ll show you a short 10­minute documentary about climate
change and bees’ ecosystem. After that, we’ll guide you in making
your very own beeswax lip balm. In addition, snacks made with
honey will be provided to all participants. There’s a 10 dollar
participation fee, and all profits will be donated to environmental
organizations. The event is limited to 100 participants, so you’d
better hurry and sign up. Don’t miss out!

questions.prompt: 다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 남자가 구입할 여행 어댑터를 고르시오.
questions.script:

M: Almost, Mom. My travel adapter is broken, so I need to buy a new
one. Could you help me choose?
W: Sure. What are your options?
M: There are five models I’m looking at. But I think anything over fifty
dollars is too expensive.
W: I agree. And maximum charging output matters, too. Don’t you like
to charge your laptop quickly?
M: Yes. So I think it should be higher than 40 watts at least.
W: Right. How about the number of USB ports?
M: I need at least four ports because I often charge multiple devices at
the same time.
W: Then, you’re down to two models. Any preference on the color?
M: The last one I used was white, so I’ll go with a different color this
time.
W: Your choice is clear, then.
M: Great. I’ll buy this one. Thanks for your help, Mom.

questions.prompt: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Daniel이 Jane에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: The app could really benefit from better visuals.
The schedule is tight, but deadlines are important too.
Most users probably won’t notice a small error like this.
Let’s deal with complaints later if people report problems.
I think we should put off the launch and fix the error first.
questions.script:
W: Daniel and Jane are part of a small team developing a new study
app. Jane is the developer and plans to launch the app next week.
Daniel, who tests the app, finds a serious problem in user settings.
Jane wants to release the app as scheduled, believing the problem
can be fixed later through an update. However, Daniel thinks that if
users experience an error right after downloading the app, they may
leave negative reviews and stop using it. He believes this could
harm the app’s success in the long run. He thinks fixing the
problem is more important than meeting the original deadline. So,
Daniel wants to suggest to Jane that they delay the launch to fix
the issue. In this situation, what would Daniel most likely say to
Jane?

M: Hello, everyone. Welcome to Today’s Insight. Many foods commonly
eaten today were not consumed in the past because they were
regarded as inedible. Here are four foods that were believed to be not
appropriate for human consumption. First, tomatoes belonged to the
same plant family as some poisonous plants. In addition, tomatoes
were believed to cause illness when they were served on metal
plates. Second, carrots were not consumed in everyday meals in the
past because of their strange colors like purple or white. Instead, they
were mainly used for animal feed. People became familiar with the
orange carrots of today only after selective farming. Next, corn also
caused worries in some European regions. People became sick when
they ate corn prepared without traditional Native­American cooking
methods. That made people believe that corn itself was unhealthy.
Finally, eggplants were once thought to be highly poisonous. Their
flowers and leaves could be harmful if eaten in large amounts. Today,
these foods are cooked properly and eaten safely. Tomorrow, we’ll
see where delicious desserts come from.
다시 한 번 듣겠습니다.
